data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":["reasoning-envelope-wf"],"disanalogies":["Logs are often append-only and linear, unlike blockchain transactions.","Self-certifying formats may not support non-deterministic or external inputs.","Proof generation may introduce unacceptable latency."],"overturn_conditions":["A simpler binding mechanism is proven to be equally effective.","The log's structure is shown to be incompatible with self-certification.","The definition of 'silent divergence' is redefined to exclude proof-based contradictions."],"shared_structure":["Zero-knowledge proofs in blockchain (e.g., Zcash, Ethereum rollups).","Digital signatures for message authentication (e.g., TLS, PGP).","Contradiction arises from proof failure (e.g., invalid signature, zk-SNARK verification error)."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_001","SRC_004"],"transfer_claims":["If zk-SNARKs ensure transaction validity, they can ensure log validity.","If digital signatures prevent message tampering, they can prevent log tampering.","If self-certifying data structures work for files, they can work for logs."]},"claim":"The durable binding is **a self-certifying log format** where each entry includes a cryptographic proof of its validity and consistency with prior entries.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The cryptographic proofs are computationally infeasible to generate or verify.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The log format is too rigid to accommodate real-world use cases.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The proofs are not publicly verifiable, limiting their utility.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The published result does not include the necessary proofs for verification.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Each log entry contains a cryptographic proof (e.g., zk-SNARK, digital signature) that it is valid and consistent with all prior entries.
